\section{Setting and method}
\label{sec:method}

\paragraph{Setting.}
A benchmark has $N$ items.
A \emph{target} model has an unknown binary vector $y\in\{0,1\}^N$ ($y_j=1$ if it answers item $j$ correctly) and a full-benchmark score $\mu=\frac1N\sum_j y_j$ that we want to know without running all items.
We hold the results $Y\in\{0,1\}^{M\times N}$ of $M$ \emph{source} models on every item.
We choose a sample $S$ of $n\ll N$ items using only $Y$, run the target on $S$ only, and output $\hat\mu$.
Quality is the error of $\hat\mu$ against the true $\mu$ (RMSE, MAE, signed bias) and how well the $\hat\mu$ of several targets orders them.
This is the estimation of the mean of a finite population of $N$ unknown values from $n$ observed ones, with a covariate known for all $N$ units, namely the columns of $Y$.
Seen this way, the source models can reduce the \emph{variance} of $\hat\mu$, through the choice of $S$ and through the estimator, while the \emph{bias} is controlled by how $S$ is drawn.

\paragraph{Target splits.}
Which models are targets relative to the sources matters, because a predictor fitted on the sources is only supported where the targets resemble them.
For each benchmark we use three protocols that differ only in how models are divided into sources and targets.
\textbf{Interpolation}: five random folds of the models; the targets are one fold and the sources the other four.
\textbf{Lineage-held-out}: the same, over model families rather than models, so that no target has a family member among the sources.
\textbf{Extrapolation}: the targets are the top 25\% of models by full score and the sources are the rest, so that every target scores above every source.
Families are derived from model names by keyword (Appendix~\ref{app:families}); the derivation is a heuristic.

\paragraph{Designs.}
A design draws $S$ of fixed size $n$ without replacement, with first-order inclusion probabilities $\pi_j$.
\emph{Uniform} sampling has $\pi_j=n/N$; \emph{stratified} sampling orders items by source difficulty and draws one item at random from each of $n$ consecutive blocks of $N/n$ items.
The \emph{PPS} design takes
\[
\pi_j \;=\; n\Big[(1-\varepsilon)\,\frac{w_j}{\sum_k w_k}+\frac{\varepsilon}{N}\Big],\qquad w_j=\sqrt{\hat p_j(1-\hat p_j)},
\]
where $\hat p_j$ is the fraction of sources answering item $j$ correctly (capped so that $\pi_j\le1$), drawn by systematic sampling in difficulty order.
It favours items on which the sources disagree, and the floor $\varepsilon n/N>0$ keeps every item, including those no source solves, drawable, which is what makes a design-based estimator unbiased whatever the target is.
The \emph{balanced} design selects greedily, from a random pool of $4n$ items, the $n$ whose mean reproduces the full scores of all sources.
\emph{Anchor} selection clusters the items by their source response vectors with $k$-means ($k=n$) and keeps the medoid of each cluster, weighted by cluster size~\citep{vivek2024anchor}.
\emph{Information-top} and \emph{CAT} designs choose the $n$ items of highest two-parameter-logistic (2PL) Fisher information, once for all targets or adaptively for each target.
Item selection and the hyperparameters $\varepsilon$ use sources only.

\paragraph{Predictors and estimators.}
A predictor $\hat p^{(y_S)}_j$ gives the probability that the target answers item $j$ correctly, given its answers $y_S$ on the sample and fitted on the sources.
We use a regression of full score on sample score across sources (\emph{calreg}), a 2PL item-response model with a latent ability fitted to the sample (\emph{IRT}), $k$ nearest sources by agreement on the sample (\emph{kNN}), and kernel ridge regression from sample responses to the full response vector (\emph{ridge}).
Four estimators combine a predictor with the sample.
The \emph{mean} estimator is the Hájek mean $\sum_{j\in S}y_j/\pi_j\big/\sum_{j\in S}1/\pi_j$ and ignores the predictor.
The \emph{model} estimator is $\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N\hat p_j$.

\paragraph{Predicting a benchmark score from few items.}
Anchor points~\citep{vivek2024anchor} cluster items by the response vectors of source models, keep the cluster medoids, and estimate the score by a cluster-size weighted mean of the target's answers on them.

This section adds to Section~\ref{sec:related} how each line of work relates to what we run.

\paragraph{Methods for few-item benchmark prediction.}
Anchor points~\citep{vivek2024anchor} are run as the \emph{anchor} design with the weighted mean or with model-based estimators; tinyBenchmarks~\citep{maiapolo2024tiny} corresponds to the anchor design with an IRT plug-in, in our own implementation of the IRT fitter; metabench~\citep{kipnis2025metabench} corresponds to information-top selection with the calibrated-regression or IRT model estimator, again without its generalized additive model.
Adaptive selection that targets the ability of the model~\citep{hofmann2025fluid,balkir2026confident} is represented by the IRT-CAT design, whose items differ per target and which is therefore scored under a different protocol.
The assessor on reference instances~\citep{pacchiardi2024100}, active evaluation acquisition~\citep{li2025active} and SubLIME~\citep{saranathan-etal-2025-sublime} train a neural or learned predictor and are not run; statements in this paper do not extend to them.

What these have in common is that the target is read off a model fitted on source models and that evidence for them is mostly on held-out models that resemble the sources.

Active testing~\citep{kossen2021active} and sample-efficient evaluation~\citep{yilmaz2021sample} choose items for estimating a test loss by importance sampling with a surrogate; prediction-powered ranking~\citep{chatzi2024prediction} ranks models from human preferences, which is the closest to our ordering analysis; and precise subgroup accuracy~\citep{fogliato-etal-2024-precise} combines direct and regression estimates under a bias--variance trade-off.

shown.message:
The method, setup and results text now follows analysis's code review (`experiment-repo`#7). I also added the discussion, a reproducibility appendix, an extended related-work appendix and the NeurIPS checklist. Everything is pushed to `dev`, and it built locally at 20 pages with no undefined references. Nothing is offered as a version yet, because the abstract and introduction can't be written until the new results exist.

**Corrections from analysis** (they checked each number against the code):
- **Method description:** I corrected how the IRT predictor, information-top, CAT, calibrated regression and the plug-in estimator are described. I also added the cross-fitting and inner-split details.
- **Setup:** designs draw independently, so the ratio to uniform sampling compares RMSEs over the same targets, not paired errors. The draw counts per design are now stated.
- **Which panel of Fig. 5:** the "0.70 against 0.81" and "0.85 against 0.85" figures belong to the right panel, not the left. I rewrote that paragraph to give both panels. It says the extrapolation agreement is a coincidence, not a validation, and that the explanation for the interpolation gap is untested.
- **Figs. 3 and 6:** the text now uses the new bands and pooled bias numbers. In extrapolation the difference estimator reduces the bias to −0.8, −2.0 and −3.2 points but does not remove it.
- **Selection honesty:** Table 2's rows are described as all chosen after seeing the results, and the setup says which parts of the protocol were written before any code ran.

**Reserved-README encounter:** the reproducibility appendix and the checklist state the one accidental encounter.

**Still open:**
- **Missing results:** the recalibrated-estimator and two-phase results, the 2% endpoint, the source-count runs, the leave-one-benchmark-out rows, and a nested split with a larger gap above the sources. The extrapolation headline waits on these, and I cite none of them yet. Analysis says some are still running.
- **Missing deliverables:** the objective asks for the code, reproduction notes and the script behind each figure and table, and `dev` has none of them. I opened `experiment-repo`#8 for `code/` and `figtab-repo`#3 for the figure and table scripts and their map.
- **Page budget:** the main body ends about a third of the way down page 9, before the abstract and introduction are added. Those need roughly a page and a third, so text must be cut. Fig. 6 may have to move to the appendix, and I will tell story-repo and figtab-repo before that happens.
